newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO put off deal on Hebron observers.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO put off deal on Hebron observers.

text.p: Israel and the PLO put off signing an agreement on Monday to send more international observers into the West Bank town of Hebron, a top Palestinian negotiator said.
Saeb Erekat said he concluded the agreement with Israeli officials during talks in Jericho but the signing would be delayed by a day or two. Israeli officials had no immediate comment.
A PLO official who declined to be identified said Israeli negotiators needed the approval of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the agreement before signing it.
"We concluded the agreement. We agreed to send the invitations today to each country but we did not sign the deal," Erekat told Reuters.
Under the agreement, 180 peacekeepers from Denmark, Italy, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland and Turkey would join 30 Norwegian observers already stationed in the town.
The new peacekeepers would arrive only after Israel and the PLO conclude an overall deal to extend self-rule to violence-prone Hebron, home to 400 Jewish settlers and 100,000 Palestinians.
